content.text: Let me look at `StringUtils.java` (547 lines) for structural opportunities.

I found a clean, safe structural improvement. `getSpecialStringForCodePoint` (lines 112–134) and `escapeWhiteSpaceChar` (lines 237–252) both define the same five whitespace escape mappings (`\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\b`, `\f`) — duplicated, drift-prone knowledge split across two methods used by different escape paths (string-literal escaping vs XML/resource escaping).

I'll make `escapeWhiteSpaceChar` the single source for whitespace escapes and have `getSpecialStringForCodePoint` delegate to it for that subset, keeping only its unique cases (`'`, `"`, `\`).

A subtlety I must preserve: `getSpecialStringForCodePoint` takes an `int` code point, while `escapeWhiteSpaceChar` takes a `char`. Casting a supplementary code point (e.g. `0x1000A`) to `char` would truncate to `0x000A` (`\n`) and wrongly escape it — so delegation must be guarded to code points that fit in a `char`.
